determine whether a requested Docupost action has a governed operation contract
inputs: a proposed Docupost outcome, adapter connection, current schema, and session identity
missing Docupost object semantics, authority, field validation, effects, privacy, cost, retry, and rollback rules
operations: inspect Docupost schema and connection metadata without transmitting a provider-domain payload
reject Docupost execution when only the generic transport shell is present and no operation-specific contract can be verified
outputs: Docupost adapter metadata
an unresolved Docupost authority and behavior contract
failureBehavior: accounts for mutable Docupost tool schemas and connection state
does not define any Docupost operation, payload, success condition, domain error, or compensating action
exclusions: does not authenticate or connect Docupost
does not execute a discovered Docupost tool
does not infer provider authority from connection availability
usefulInvariants: Docupost schemas are inspected before use
Docupost effects remain blocked until a domain contract and authority are explicit
materialRisks: Docupost schemas can expose consequential write operations
Docupost authentication can grant broad account access
Docupost requests may disclose sensitive data or incur cost

reviews.neutralCapabilitySummary: Outlines an AI-agent delivery lifecycle from purpose and success criteria through tool, memory, single or multi-agent architecture, state orchestration, implementation, safety, evaluation, and deployment, while delegating most detail to assumed companion skills and named frameworks.
neutralIntentExamples: derive the minimum agent architecture from a real workflow
evaluate whether an agent needs tools, memory, or multiple workers
inputs: user workflow and success criteria, environment, deterministic alternatives, model and tool capabilities, effect and authority boundaries, state and memory needs, privacy, latency and cost budget, failure modes, evaluation corpus, deployment, and rollback
prompt injection, tool misuse, memory privacy, model drift, multi-agent overhead, framework lock-in, retries and duplicate effects, observability, human escalation, and external action authority
operations: model the user workflow and prove where an agent adds value over deterministic software
select the smallest architecture and define typed tool, state, memory, authority, and failure contracts
implement incrementally and evaluate representative outcomes, safety, cost, latency, degradation, and rollback before deployment
outputs: agent architecture and implementation plan
tool, memory, state, authority, and failure contracts
evaluation, safety, cost, and deployment evidence
failureBehavior: the source is a broad checklist coupled to assumed skills
framework-first selection overbuilds simple workflows
memory and multiple agents amplify privacy and cost
generic quality gates do not prove behavior
exclusions: does not choose a framework before requirements
does not add memory or agents without measured need
does not grant broad tool authority
does not deploy from checklist completion
does not treat model output as proof
does not omit deterministic fallback
